definitions.explanation: Music of Japanese origin, especially traditional forms played on instruments such as the koto, shamisen, and shakuhachi. Contrasts with 洋楽 (Western music).

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}の{邦楽|ほうがく}サークルで{琴|こと}を{弾|ひ}いている。
examples.english: I play the koto in my university's Japanese music club.

examples.japanese: この{音楽祭|おんがくさい}では、{邦楽|ほうがく}と{洋楽|ようがく}の{両方|りょうほう}を{楽|たの}しむことができる。
examples.english: At this music festival, you can enjoy both Japanese and Western music.

notes:
USAGE:
{邦楽|ほうがく} primarily refers to traditional Japanese music genres such as {雅楽|ががく} (court music), {能楽|のうがく} (Noh music), {長唄|ながうた} (a shamisen vocal genre), and {箏曲|そうきょく} (koto music). In some contexts, it may also include modern Japanese popular music (J-pop), though the traditional meaning is more common.

CONTRAST:
- {邦楽|ほうがく}: Japanese music
- {洋楽|ようがく}: Western music

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {邦楽|ほうがく}{器|き} (traditional Japanese musical instrument)
- {邦楽|ほうがく}{演奏|えんそう} (performance of Japanese music)
- {邦楽|ほうがく}サークル (Japanese music club)

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
Do not confuse with {方角|ほうがく} (direction, compass bearing), which shares the same reading.
